# Cubic phase and affine state controls

Original primitive controls generated by `tools/svg_cubic_state_controls.py`.
Eight independently authored integer curves each have a whole representation
and two exact halves. Five fractional shifts produce 120 cases; four scales
and four signed/axis-swapped transforms produce another 384. Rational Bernstein
evaluation at four parameters proves each half's polynomial identity. Every
input coordinate lies on the 1/16 lattice. No corpus artwork or font program.

Generate inputs in a scratch directory, then capture with
`tools/capture-cubic-flatten-sweep.ps1 -QuantizeInput`. Record using the authoring
tool's `--native CAPTURE_JSON` option. Gzip payloads have zero timestamps and
their hashes, source hashes and capture/input binding are in `reference.json`.
The native API uses GraphicsPath.Flatten(null, 0.25); these observations are
separate from the native DOCX picture evidence in `svg-cubic-phase`.

All 120 native fractional-phase contours translate exactly. The existing
renderer matches 402/504 contours; the experimental p6-even midpoint model
matches 344/504. Native whole/split equality depends on scale and representation,
despite identical polynomials. This rules out a simple integer-input switch.

The unit regression protects the 402 currently correct native contours and
fractional translation invariance. It allows the remaining contours to improve.
The candidate model is diagnostic only and is never imported by the application.
Its perfect 40 phase whole-curves have right-half native counterexamples.
